blocks.md: A journal turns an unreliable sequence of device writes into a recoverable history. Records need boundaries, ordering, and integrity so recovery can distinguish a valid prefix from a torn tail or real corruption.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: Append gives a record an LSN, but only Sync makes the requested prefix durable. Recovery trusts structure and checksum, not intent.

blocks.title: Recover the longest valid prefix
blocks.md: Scan frames in LSN order and apply only records proven complete and valid. A partial final frame is a torn tail; a complete frame with a bad checksum or sequence gap is corruption.

blocks.label: What you implement
blocks.code: func OpenJournal(dir string, device contract.Device) (contract.Journal, error)

blocks.input:
frame 1: valid
frame 2: valid
frame 3: header + half payload
blocks.explain: The third frame declares bytes that are not present, so it was interrupted at the end. Recovery keeps the proven prefix and reports the tail condition without inventing record 3.

items: LSNs start at one, increase by one, and unknown Sync targets return `ErrUnknownLSN`.
CRC-32 covers every frame byte before the checksum field.
Reject oversized lengths before allocation and stop at sequence gaps or checksum failures.
`Close` is terminal and idempotent; propagate errors returned by the recovery callback.

items.title: Encode one exact frame
items.md: Write fixed-width fields in the documented byte order and compute CRC over the same bytes recovery will verify.

items.title: Separate appended from durable
items.md: Track assigned LSNs independently from the Device's flushed boundary.

items.title: Classify the stopping point
items.md: Clean end, torn tail, tail garbage, and corruption have deliberately different outcomes.

blocks.title: Where performance comes from
blocks.md: Correct framing comes first. Then batch durability behind `Sync` and recover incrementally so append throughput rises without reading or allocating the whole journal.
